Manchester: Gateway to Britain's Best Riding

Manchester is arguably the best-placed city in Britain for motorcycle touring. Within an hour, you can be riding the Cat and Fiddle, climbing Snake Pass, or crossing into North Wales. Within two hours, you're in the Lake District, Yorkshire Dales, or Snowdonia. No other British city offers such concentration of world-class riding.

1. Peak District Circuit (70 miles)

The quickest escape from Manchester. Take the A537 Cat and Fiddle to Buxton, continue through the Hope Valley past Mam Tor, over Snake Pass back towards Glossop, and return via the A57. This 70-mile loop covers the Peak District's highlights and can be ridden as an evening blast in summer or a full morning with stops.

2. Yorkshire Dales Weekend (200 miles)

Head east on the M62 then A629 to Skipton, the Dales gateway. Spend a day riding Buttertubs Pass, Fleet Moss, and the B-roads through Swaledale and Wensleydale. Stay overnight in Hawes or Leyburn. Return via Ribblehead Viaduct and the A65 through Settle.

3. Lake District Adventure (180 miles)

The M6 north to Kendal takes 90 minutes, then you're into the Lake District proper. Tackle Hardknott and Wrynose Passes, circle Ullswater, and explore the western lakes via Honister Pass. Stay in Keswick or Ambleside. Return via the A6 through the Lune Gorge for a different perspective.

4. North Wales Blast (150 miles)

Head south-west on the A55 into Snowdonia. The Evo Triangle (A543, A5, B4501) is barely 90 minutes from Manchester and offers some of Wales' best roads. Extend to the Llanberis Pass and Black Rock Sands for a full weekend. The roads are quieter than the Peak District and equally dramatic.

Manchester riders are spoilt for choice. The Peak District for after-work blasts, the Dales for Saturday rides, the Lakes for full weekends, and Wales for something different. It's motorcycling paradise.

5. Forest of Bowland (100 miles)

The Trough of Bowland is Lancashire's hidden gem. Head north on the M6 to Lancaster, then east into the Forest of Bowland AONB. The Trough road climbs through a dramatic glacial valley with minimal traffic. Combine with the Ribble Valley villages of Clitheroe and Whalley for a full day. This area is seriously underrated.

Practical Tips

  • Peak District: Accessible year-round, busiest on weekends. Midweek evenings are golden
  • Yorkshire: Best April-October. Book Dales accommodation early in summer
  • Lake District: Avoid August bank holiday at all costs. May and September are ideal
  • North Wales: Friday evening departure gets you to Snowdonia for Saturday morning riding
keyTakeaways: Manchester is arguably Britain's best-placed touring base: the Peak District, Dales, Lakes and Snowdonia are all within easy reach.
Quick hits include the 70-mile Peak District Circuit over the Cat and Fiddle and Snake Pass, ideal for a summer evening blast.
Bigger weekends run to the Yorkshire Dales (200 miles), Lake District (180 miles) and North Wales (150 miles).
The Forest of Bowland and its Trough road are a seriously underrated 100-mile day out.
Avoid the Lake District on August bank holiday; May and September are ideal.

faq.q: What is the quickest ride from Manchester?
faq.a: The 70-mile Peak District Circuit is the fastest escape. Take the A537 Cat and Fiddle to Buxton, ride the Hope Valley past Mam Tor, cross Snake Pass towards Glossop and return on the A57. It works as an evening blast in summer or a full morning with stops, packing the Peak's highlights into a compact loop right on the city's doorstep.

faq.q: Which weekend needs an overnight stay?
faq.a: The Yorkshire Dales at 200 miles and the Lake District at 180 miles both reward an overnight. In the Dales, stay in Hawes or Leyburn after riding Buttertubs Pass and Fleet Moss. In the Lakes, base yourself in Keswick or Ambleside to tackle Hardknott, Wrynose and Honister. Book Dales and Lakes beds early in summer, as they fill quickly.

faq.q: Where is the best North Wales riding from Manchester?
faq.a: Head south-west on the A55 into Snowdonia. The Evo Triangle, formed by the A543, A5 and B4501, is barely 90 minutes away and offers some of Wales' best roads. Extend to the Llanberis Pass and Black Rock Sands for a full weekend. The roads here are quieter than the Peak District and just as dramatic.

faq.q: When should I avoid the Lake District?
faq.a: Steer clear of the August bank holiday, when holiday traffic, campervans and inexperienced drivers make the passes frustrating. May and September deliver the best balance of settled weather and quieter roads. A Friday-evening departure via the M6 to Kendal sets you up for a full Saturday of riding before the crowds arrive.

faq.q: Is the Forest of Bowland worth the trip?
faq.a: Absolutely, and it is seriously underrated. Head north on the M6 to Lancaster, then east into the Forest of Bowland AONB. The Trough of Bowland climbs through a dramatic glacial valley with minimal traffic. Combine it with the Ribble Valley villages of Clitheroe and Whalley for a satisfying 100-mile day away from the busier honeypots.
